objective: Scrub credential-shaped payload keys and raw-evidence fields out of the /timeline and /events response bodies through the versioned redaction module, record the rule version when a value changed, and leave the append-only source event and its correlation fields unmodified.
decision_supported: May the read-only backend serve a producer-controlled event payload over /timeline and /events, or must the response copy clear the same artifact boundary every other scrubbed artifact clears?
acceptance: /timeline response payloads scrub credential-shaped keys and raw-evidence fields through workbench.application.redaction rather than a second scheme
/events response payloads and the run summary derived from them clear the same boundary through the same module
a clean payload is returned unchanged and run_id, sequence_no, event_id, event_type, occurred_at and evidence_refs survive verbatim
the HTTP body of both routes never contains the synthetic credential or the raw-frame sentinel
a scrubbed item carries redaction.rules == REDACTION_RULES_VERSION with a bounded redacted_values count, and a clean item carries no marker
the append-only source event, its in-memory record and the .jsonl on disk are byte-identical before and after both reads
evidence: reproducer after: run_timeline returns {'api_key': '<redacted>', 'raw_frame': '<evidence-ref:redacted>'}' with redaction.rules == redaction-rules-v1
HTTP-level assertion on /api/v1/runs/{run_id}/timeline and /events that the sentinels are absent from the decoded body
clean-payload equality assertion and an assertion that a clean item grows no redaction marker
byte-equality assertion on the source .jsonl before and after both routes are read
stop_conditions: the API cannot distinguish an evidence reference from raw evidence without a contract change
a fix would filter a field silently instead of reporting the withheld value in band
the change would mutate the append-only event store or rewrite a stored event
the redaction module would have to be duplicated, forked or diverged from REDACTION_RULES_VERSION
data_classification: synthetic-only fixture values; no live credential, camera frame or personal data is introduced or read
model_policy: No model call is made by the change or by its tests.
risks_and_fallbacks: A clean payload must stay byte-identical, so the redactor is applied per response object and the marker is added only when a count is non-zero
Rollback is to mark the timeline payload unavailable and return evidence_refs only; the disable path fails closed and never serves the unredacted payload
The OpenAPI schema describes payload as a free-form object, so a bounded redaction marker is additive and needs no contract change
